problem: How could a professional services firm grow when AI does the drafting?

dims.note: How rule-bound or unruly the idea is.
Whether it earns its place by use or by feeling.
How far it departs from what people expect.
How many people it is for.
Whether growth comes from medieval-style masters and apprentices or from industrial-scale standard output.
Whether clients pay for stripped-back clarity or for rich, ornate, visibly hand-finished work.
Borrow speed and telemetry from racing teams, or taste and signature from top restaurants.
Whether the firm hides the work or turns sign-off and judgement into a ritual clients value.

ideas.title: Sell advice, not drafts
ideas.desc: Let AI write the first drafts and move staff time to judgement, client advice and relationships, priced by outcome instead of by the hour.

mainstream.r: Fits any firm of any size

dm0vu01.r: Keeps craft judgement, automates the rest

ideas.t1750why: Many firms are already doing this today.

ideas.title: Fixed price document subscription
ideas.desc: Offer unlimited standard documents for a flat monthly fee, produced by AI and checked by a small review team within hours.
ideas.t1750why: Already offered by some legal and accounting firms.

ideas.title: Partner signs in person
ideas.desc: Every major piece of work ends with a senior partner reading it aloud to the client and signing it by hand at a formal meeting.

dm0vu84.r: It is literally a signing ceremony

ideas.t1750why: Old fashioned but perfectly believable as a premium service.

ideas.title: Insure every answer
ideas.desc: Back each piece of advice with a cash guarantee, so clients buy the firm's willingness to pay if it is wrong.

dm0vu84.r: The guarantee is a visible pledge

ideas.t1750why: Unusual, though warranties on advice exist in small ways.

ideas.title: One trade, total depth
ideas.desc: Serve a single tiny sector, such as independent vets, and know its people, rules and gossip better than any model could.
ideas.t1750why: Narrow specialist firms are common and sensible.

ideas.title: Live drafting room
ideas.desc: Clients sit with the team for an hour while AI drafts on a big screen and everyone argues the document into shape together.

order.r: Messy, open argument in the room

predictable.r: Clients rarely see the work made

dm0vu63.r: Fast, timed, crew around one job

ideas.t1750why: Workshops exist, but live drafting as the product is rare.

ideas.title: Pay clients for disagreement
ideas.desc: Give clients a refund whenever they catch the firm's AI out, turning each error into a public league table of sharp clients.

predictable.r: Rewarding fault finding is very unusual

dm0vu22.r: A league table is pure flourish

ideas.t1750why: Publishing your own errors as a game sounds reckless today.

ideas.title: The unwritten firm
ideas.desc: Stop producing documents altogether and sell only spoken counsel, given face to face, with nothing recorded and nothing for a machine to copy.

order.r: No paper trail to rely on

predictable.r: A firm with no documents is startling

ideas.t1750why: Regulators and clients expect written records of everything.

ideas.title: License the firm's brain
ideas.desc: Train a model on decades of the firm's past work and rent it to rival firms and in house teams as a product.

predictable.r: Selling to rivals is a small twist

ideas.t1750why: Plausible, but client confidentiality makes it hard today.

ideas.title: Bespoke illuminated contracts
ideas.desc: Hire calligraphers and illustrators to turn key agreements into handmade keepsakes that founders frame, celebrating the deal as much as recording it.

dm0vu84.r: Made for the moment of signing

ideas.t1750why: Charming but most would find it a strange growth plan.

ideas.title: Midnight contract vending machine
ideas.desc: Clients answer ten questions on a kiosk or app and get a finished, checked document in four minutes, any hour.
ideas.t1750why: Online document tools already come close to this.

ideas.title: Acquire rivals for their clients
ideas.desc: Buy small firms that cannot afford the AI shift, keep their client relationships and run the work through one shared drafting system.
ideas.t1750why: Roll-ups are already ordinary in professional services.

ideas.title: The apprentice table
ideas.desc: Each client gets a named master and two apprentices who learn their business for years and hand-finish every AI draft.

function.r: Loyalty matters as much as output

mainstream.r: Suits clients who pay for care

ideas.t1750why: Close to how good firms once worked.

ideas.title: Red team for hire
ideas.desc: Sell a service where a rowdy team attacks the client's AI-drafted documents and plans, hunting for the flaw that sinks them.
ideas.t1750why: Red teaming exists, though rarely for advice work.

ideas.title: The firm that grieves with you
ideas.desc: Specialise in the worst moments, such as insolvency, divorce and death, with advisers trained as counsellors while AI handles all paperwork.
ideas.t1750why: Unusual, but nobody would call it mad.

ideas.title: Deal day festival
ideas.desc: Turn each closing into a staged public event with music, witnesses, speeches and a printed keepsake, sold as a premium package.
ideas.t1750why: A law or accounting firm as events company sounds odd.

ideas.title: Random partner roulette
ideas.desc: Every month clients are paired by lottery with an expert from an unrelated practice who reviews their business and suggests one wild move.
ideas.t1750why: Paying for randomly assigned advice sounds reckless today.

ideas.title: Invisible compliance layer
ideas.desc: Plug the firm's rules into client software so contracts, filings and checks happen in the background with no meetings at all.
ideas.t1750why: Embedded compliance tools are emerging already.

ideas.title: One document a year
ideas.desc: Take only twelve clients and spend a full month each on one perfect, career-defining agreement, priced like a commissioned artwork.

predictable.r: Scarcity is rare in this trade

dm0vu63.r: A tasting menu of one dish

ideas.t1750why: Growing by serving twelve clients sounds backwards.

ideas.title: Clients own the firm
ideas.desc: Convert to a cooperative where clients hold shares, vote on what the firm builds and split the savings AI creates.

mainstream.r: Could suit many, tried by few

ideas.t1750why: Partnership rules make client ownership hard to imagine today.

ideas.title: Train every junior as adviser
ideas.desc: Move juniors off drafting and into client meetings from their first year, so the firm sells more judgement per head.
ideas.t1750why: Already happening in many firms.

ideas.title: Thousand small clients
ideas.desc: Use cheap AI drafting to serve small businesses that could never afford the firm before, at very high volume.
ideas.t1750why: Online legal services already do a version of this.

ideas.title: Ten minute turnaround guarantee
ideas.desc: Promise any standard document reviewed and returned within ten minutes, timed publicly, with a refund if the clock is missed.
ideas.t1750why: Ambitious but believable with current tools.

ideas.title: Lifelong family counsel
ideas.desc: One named adviser stays with a family or founder for decades, handling every matter and knowing their whole history.
ideas.t1750why: Family solicitors and private banks have long done this.

ideas.title: Publish every template free
ideas.desc: Give away all the firm's documents and prompts openly, then charge only for the hard cases that people bring back.
ideas.t1750why: Common in software, still rare and worrying for firms.

ideas.title: Advice as theatre
ideas.desc: Stage each major client decision as a performed hearing with advocates, a jury of peers and a verdict the board watches live.
ideas.t1750why: Sounds like a stunt to most serious clients.

ideas.title: Bet fees on outcomes
ideas.desc: Take no fee for the work and instead take a share of the result, such as the deal value or the tax saved.
ideas.t1750why: Contingency fees exist, but not across all work.

ideas.title: Firm for one village
ideas.desc: Serve only one small town, knowing every business, family and dispute in it, and become its trusted memory.

predictable.r: Odd answer to a growth question

ideas.t1750why: Old fashioned, but strange as a growth plan.

ideas.title: Swarm of client agents
ideas.desc: Give every client an AI agent that negotiates with other clients' agents all day, with the firm only setting the rules.
ideas.t1750why: Machines striking binding deals unsupervised still alarms most people.

ideas.title: Handwritten letter of advice
ideas.desc: Deliver every conclusion as a single handwritten letter from a partner, sealed and carried to the client by hand.
ideas.t1750why: Charming but looks wilfully backward to most clients.

ideas.title: Sell the audit trail
ideas.desc: Charge clients for a checked record showing who reviewed each AI draft, what changed and why.

predictable.r: A natural next step for firms

mainstream.r: Most regulated clients would want it

ideas.t1750why: Review logs are already common in regulated work.

ideas.title: Fewer people, bigger mandates
ideas.desc: Shrink drafting teams and use the freed partner time to chase larger, more complex engagements.

predictable.r: What most firms will try first

ideas.t1750why: Firms are already doing this.

ideas.title: White label drafting plant
ideas.desc: Run a high volume AI drafting operation that smaller firms rent under their own names.
ideas.t1750why: Outsourced back offices exist, though rarely at this scale.

ideas.title: The slow firm
ideas.desc: Promise that every piece of advice takes at least thirty days of human thought before delivery.

order.r: Fixed rule, but against the grain

predictable.r: Slowness as a selling point is odd

mainstream.r: Only a few clients will wait

ideas.t1750why: Paying more for deliberate delay sounds perverse to most buyers.

ideas.title: Jury of strangers
ideas.desc: Test each piece of advice on a paid panel of random members of the public before the client sees it.

mainstream.r: Suits disputes and public facing work

dm0vu22.r: Adds an extra layer of show

dm0vu63.r: Tasting panel more than pit crew

ideas.t1750why: Confidentiality rules make outsiders reviewing advice sound reckless.

ideas.title: Annual client pilgrimage
ideas.desc: Take every client away once a year for a walking retreat where all major decisions are talked through.

order.r: Loose talk on an open road

ideas.t1750why: Retreats exist but not as the main service.

ideas.title: Drafts auctioned by the minute
ideas.desc: Let clients bid in a live market for instant partner review slots on AI drafts, with prices moving all day.

predictable.r: Surge pricing for advice is new

dm0vu63.r: Seconds matter, like a pit stop

ideas.t1750why: Bidding for a partner's attention feels undignified to the profession.

ideas.title: The oath book
ideas.desc: Each adviser swears a public, recorded oath on every major opinion, kept in a bound book clients can visit.

predictable.r: Oaths feel out of their time

dm0vu01.r: Personal pledge by a named master

ideas.t1750why: Sworn oaths over routine opinions would seem theatrical and odd.

ideas.title: Advice only for beekeepers
ideas.desc: Serve one tiny trade worldwide, with AI drafting in every language and advisers who keep bees themselves.

order.r: Focused, but a scattered client base

mainstream.r: About as narrow as it gets

dm0vu01.r: Advisers are practitioners of the craft

ideas.t1750why: Micro niches exist but a global one this small is rare.

ideas.title: No office, no names
ideas.desc: Offer anonymous machine checked advice through a plain text box, with no people, brand or meetings shown at all.
ideas.t1750why: Trusting advice from a firm with no named adviser still alarms people.

ideas.title: Sell the checking, not drafting
ideas.desc: Let clients draft with their own AI, then charge a fixed fee to review, correct and stand behind the result with the firm's insurance.

order.r: Fixed process, but client drafts vary widely

predictable.r: Logical step, yet few firms offer it

mainstream.r: Most clients with AI tools could use it

dm0vu01.r: Repeatable review with some expert judgement

dm0vu22.r: Plain fixed fee service, no frills

dm0vu63.r: Quick turnaround matters more than polish

dm0vu84.r: The firm's sign off is the product

ideas.t1750why: Review services exist already, only the client drafting is new.

ideas.title: Juniors placed inside clients
ideas.desc: Since drafting no longer trains juniors, second them into client teams for a fee to learn the business and spot new work early.

order.r: Planned scheme, but placements unfold loosely

function.r: Solves training and sales, some relationship warmth

predictable.r: Secondments are known, the scale is new

mainstream.r: Works for most firms and clients

dm0vu63.r: Slow craft learning over rapid turnaround

dm0vu84.r: Human presence, though without much ritual

ideas.t1750why: Secondments are common, making them the main training route is unusual.

ideas.title: Weekly client problem sweep
ideas.desc: Use the hours saved on drafting to scan each client's contracts, filings and news weekly, then send a short list of issues worth fixing.

order.r: Regular rhythm, but findings are unpredictable

function.r: Practical alerts that create paid work

predictable.r: Sensible extension of existing client care

mainstream.r: Suits nearly any firm with retained clients

dm0vu22.r: A short plain list each week

dm0vu63.r: Speed and regular timing matter most

ideas.t1750why: Monitoring services already exist in several professional fields.

function:2|order:2|predictable:0@3.why: A firm that is both chaotic and emotional will always surprise people. Predictable chaos stops being chaos, so ideas here cancel themselves out.

function:1|order:2|predictable:0@3.why: Disorder that everyone can foresee is just routine with a messy name. Nothing chaotic stays predictable for long in client work.

function:0|order:2|predictable:0@3.why: Loose, unmanaged freelance pools doing routine work could function, but firms sell reliability and clients distrust anything that looks disorganised.

function:0|order:1|predictable:1@3.why: Middling, practical moves with a slight twist get little attention. Talk about AI in firms favours either safe efficiency plays or bold reinventions, so the sensible middle stays empty.

function:2|order:2|predictable:1@3.why: Loose, feeling-led ideas of middling novelty, such as open house client days or drop-in clinics, could work. Nobody has yet looked here.

function:0|order:1|predictable:0@3.why: This is the home of ordinary efficiency moves like cross-selling and price cuts. Too obvious to list, so the map skipped them.

function:2|order:0|predictable:0@3.why: Steady, ritual client care such as birthday calls and annual lunches works well, but it seems old fashioned next to talk of AI.

function:2|order:1|predictable:0@3.why: Familiar relationship building, like client dinners and friendly check-ins, still wins work. It is seen as dull and hard to measure, so it gets ignored.

stops.title: Locked template sign-off
stops.desc: Clients may only draft inside the firm's approved AI templates, and a fixed checklist review then stamps and insures each document.
stops.t1750why: Document automation with sign-off already exists.
stops.note: Clients no longer draft with their own AI, so it becomes the firm's drafting product.

stops.title: Tiered review menu
stops.desc: Clients draft with any AI, submit through a set intake form, and pay a fixed fee by document type for insured review.
stops.t1750why: Fixed fee review is familiar; the AI source is new.

stops.title: Open door review
stops.desc: Clients send any AI draft in any state, and the firm quotes a fixed fee on sight to fix and insure it.

predictable.r: Quoting on sight is less usual

stops.t1750why: Insuring unknown machine drafts on sight feels slightly bold.

stops.title: Live draft patrol
stops.desc: Reviewers sit inside the client's AI tools on a flat subscription, correcting and vouching for drafts as they change during live deals.

order.r: No fixed scope or final version

dm0vu84.r: Vouching happens quietly in the flow

stops.t1750why: Insurers covering ever changing drafts sounds hard to arrange.
stops.note: Fixed fee becomes a subscription and cover gets strained, but checking is still the product.

stops.title: Vouch for everything
stops.desc: The firm stands behind whatever any client's AI produces, in any form, at any time, with no intake, scope or set review.

mainstream.r: Only reckless buyers would trust it

stops.t1750why: No insurer would cover unbounded, unreviewed machine output.
stops.note: Without scope or a set review, nothing can be priced, insured or honestly stood behind.

stretches.summary: It breaks at both ends: full order takes drafting back from the client, full chaos makes the guarantee uninsurable. The idea needs free drafting but a bounded sign-off.

trail.text: Filled the unfashionable gap (between Order and Chaos · Function · between Predictable and Surprising) with 3 ideas.
Stretched Sell the checking, not drafting along Order ↔ Chaos. It breaks at −1.0 and +1.0.
